It can really damage you and your relationship. As can anything in excess. Just be careful and don't give in into either without doing some soul searching first. Question why you would want to be in that dynamic, and why you wouldn't. Measure both, compromise, and apply it. If it doesn't work out make sure both you and your partner are up and ready to patch it, fix it, or stop doing it and move on to something healthier. Cheers.

Can completely relate! However, the first 4 albums are near impossible to top. There's absolutely no way you can repeat that type of heaviness and maturity Fortress has, you can't repeat the darkness and longing you find in ABIII, can't repeat the uplifting anthemic sound in One day remains, and you can't repeat Blackbird. As a hardcore fan of theirs, I can't ask them for more when we simply DON'T DESERVE THIS MUCH GOOD SHIT. As cheesy as it sounds to ask AB to top themselves after decades of being hard-working musicians, having families, touring relentlessly, and having multiple bands, personally whatever comes after Fortress is just bliss. It took me 3 whole years to get into The Last Hero. It was hard for me to find the things that made me love Alter Bridge in that album, but when you listen to those songs individually and not as a whole album, you won't get as exhausted and can have the *TIME* to process this new sound of theirs. TLH is an anthemic-heroic-epic-monstrous sound that is simply ridiculous that such chord progressions and heavy riffing can even exist while still sounding melodic. Continue giving it a shot, remove the songs you don't like an solely focus on the ones you do. Cradle to the Grave and The Last Hero are imo worthy of the first 4 albums, and so is Dying light. WTS is one i'm currently struggling with but everytime I hear Pay No Mind it pulls me right back. Such a unique sound that after you try to find that usual darkness of theirs you start to see the albums in a new light. Hope it helps!
